summary: Iteration 7: full-stack testing of the on-site defect logging feature. Backend: 11 pytest tests (defect CRUD, photo upload/download, pack.html embedding, 404/422 validation, 401 auth guards on all 4 defect endpoints, plus auth playbook checks) — all passing. Frontend: end-to-end Playwright run on /project/RTF-2026-0142/design/defects covering nav item, summary/empty state, add (save disabled until description non-empty), photo attach, edit (pre-filled form), delete, and reload persistence at every step; Design Pack preview confirmed to render the added defect with embedded photo under Section 08. All test data cleaned up (all 8 projects back to 0 defects, orphan Defect Photo documents removed).

minor.issue: Deleting a defect does not soft/hard-delete the associated 'Defect Photo' document. The uploaded photo stays in db.documents and therefore keeps appearing in GET /api/projects/{id}/documents (Evidence tab) and in object storage — orphaned data grows with every delete/replace.

Replacing a photo overwrites d['photo'] without deleting the previous document (same orphan issue). Also no size/mime whitelist enforcement beyond the extension fallback — a non-image file named .png is accepted and stored.
doc_type 'Defect Photo' is not filtered out of the project document list, so defect photos surface in the Evidence/document list alongside real evidence uploads (may be intentional — confirm).

issues: Minor: the 'Replace photo' camera icon button on a card with a photo has no data-testid (only the initial 'defect-attach-{id}' does), so photo replacement is not directly automatable.
Minor: no confirmation dialog on defect delete — a single click on the trash icon permanently removes the defect with no undo.

action_items: Clean up the defect photo document (db.documents record + stored object) when a defect is deleted or its photo replaced, otherwise orphaned 'Defect Photo' docs accumulate and show in the project documents/Evidence list.
Optional: add data-testid to the 'Replace photo' button and a confirm step before defect delete.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py delete_defect(): remove/soft-delete the linked document (d['photoDocId']) inside the same handler to keep documents and storage consistent.
server.py upload_defect_photo(): validate content_type against an image whitelist and cap file size; currently the extension is silently coerced to .jpg for unknown types and any payload is stored.
server.py is 2175 lines — well past the 700-line guideline; pack HTML building (build_pack_html/_render_pack_html) and the project/defect routers should be split into modules.

auth.py seed_admins() intentionally never overwrites an existing admin password (documented in a comment). This deviates from the playbook expectation that seed updates the hash when the seeded password changes — confirm this is the desired behaviour, otherwise a rotated seed password will silently not take effect.
seed_data_creation: One temporary defect + PNG photo on RTF-2026-0142 (created via UI and via pytest). All removed afterwards; verified all 8 projects have 0 defects and no 'Defect Photo' documents remain.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Defect feature (backend + frontend) verified end-to-end in iteration 7; regression suite is /app/backend/tests/test_iter7_defects.py (loadscope-safe: all stateful tests live in TestDefectCrud so xdist keeps them on one worker). Auth playbook verified: bcrypt hashes are $2b$, login sets httpOnly+Secure+SameSite=None cookies, lockout returns 429 after 5 failed attempts (15 min, keyed per email — use a random email in tests to avoid a stale lock), app-level CORS echoes the request Origin with allow-credentials=true (the preview edge proxy rewrites ACAO to '*' on the public URL, so assert CORS on the internal port or leniently). Design Pack: explicit defects REPLACE the risk-derived fallback rows in Section 08 (by design); RTF-2026-0142 shows 5 fallback rows when it has no defects.
rca_of_the_issue: No functional defects found. The only real finding is an orphaned-data bug: upload_defect_photo() inserts a db.documents record and stores an object, but delete_defect() only filters the defect out of project.defects, leaving the document and stored file behind (reproduced: after add->photo->delete, GET /api/projects/{id}/documents still lists the 'Defect Photo'). Fix by deleting/soft-deleting photoDocId on defect delete and on photo replace.
